## Description

The blue trumpet (pigment stentorin), extending up to ~1 mm. It attaches by its foot; the crown of
membranelles creates a vortex that brings bacteria and small algae. Touched, hit by a sudden current or
a sudden increase of light (stentorin is its photoreceptor), its myonemes shorten the whole cell in
milliseconds; it re-extends in seconds. Contracted it is an almost spherical pear; attached and
extended, a trumpet. When hungry it lets go, swims as a pear and reattaches.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.22), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 2 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

A contracted body of ~200 µm with [whole-body contraction](../../mechanics/shape-changes.md) (`profile = "trumpet"`:
oral disc, conical body and a thin peduncle ending in the foot, with the mouth width from volume
conservation), triggered by touch, shear or light responses and spontaneously. A
[foot](../../mechanics/stalks-and-colonies.md) instead of a stalk. Stentorin stripes drawn. Extended length, foot
width, re-extension time, spontaneous contractions and thresholds estimated.

## Not implemented yet

- No habituation or hierarchy of responses.
- Real extended length (~1 mm) is not reached; no regeneration from fragments.
- No measured µmax.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Shares whole-body contraction with the peritrich zooids and pigment stripes with *Blepharisma*.
